newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg/mark eyes recovery above 3.0 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg/mark eyes recovery above 3.0 marks.

text.p: Sterling is poised to claw back some of its losses after collapsing through trendline support and below 3.0 marks in early Europe, said chartists.

"We have bounced back a little this morning and we could go further...But there is going to be some trendline resistance coming in around 3.0140 marks," said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank.
"We may see a bounce-back towards there, but if we fail below there (3.0140), then certainly the pressure will be kept very much on the downside," said Stannard.
At 0745 GMT, sterling/mark stood at 3.0010/20 marks.
This compared with 3.0130/40 marks in late Europe on Monday, though it was off lows around 2.9885 seen in early Europe.
Against the mark, sterling has lost more than seven pfennigs from its high of 3.0627 marks on Monday to troughs of 2.9885 visited in early Europe on Tuesday.
But despite the sharp slide, chartists said the move did not signify the beginning of the end for sterling nor a meltdown.
"At this stage, there is not enough evidence to suggest this is the end of the entire upmove," said Stannard.
Chartists said while the price action was not fatal, it renders sterling vulnerable.
